text_blocks.snippet: Central Illinois residents face active scams including fake DMV/Tollway text messages, impostor local repair services, and business directory verification calls. Con artists also target college rental markets and use AI-driven impersonation tactics to steal money or personal details.
snippet_highlighted_words: fake DMV/Tollway text messages, impostor local repair services, and business directory verification calls

list.snippet: Fake DMV & Toll Texts: Fraudulent SMS messages claim you owe money for unpaid tolls or state tickets, threatening license suspension if you click the link.
Impostor Repair Services: Scammers use fake search engine listings and mimic legitimate local garage door or home service companies, overcharging drastically or damaging equipment.
Google Listing Calls: Callers pose as Google Business support, threatening local shops with unverified status or lost rankings unless they pay an urgent verification fee.
Rental & Housing Fraud: Fake landlords copy real property listings to grab deposits and first-month rent from students and movers.
AI & Family Impersonation: Scammers use voice tools or artificial intelligence to pretend to be distressed family members or officials demanding immediate payment.
Practice the pause: Stop and think before acting on urgent requests for money or personal data.

Do not click links:
Never open unexpected text or email links about tolls, packages, or fees.
Verify independently: Look up official phone numbers separately rather than trusting caller ID or top search results.

Report suspicious activity:
Check or file reports with the Better Business Bureau of Central Illinois.
